text_fidelity_a: Faber-Castell Do-Art Dot a Design Animals For ages 6 and up. The set comes with 6 "design sheets" for kids to paint, but there are only 3 designs (koala, turtle, or dolphin). You get one sheet with only black-and-white lines for an older child to paint and dot. You also get that same design with the main colors pre-printed and you only need to add dots of paint to the white dots in the design. The kit also comes with: 8 acrylic paints (light blue, dark blue, green, yellow-green, yellow, orange, red, purple), 2 fine tip dotters, 1 medium tip dotter, 1 brush, sticky tac (keeps paper flat while painting), 2 cardboard frames with hangers, and instructions. Acrylic paints can dry out quickly, so you may need to add water to the paints to keep them from drying out. Acrylic paints can quickly dry onto clothing and not come out, so you'll want to wear a painting smock. Wash dotters, brush (and work surface) before the paint dries if you intend to reuse them. The "dotters" are foam rounds on the end of a handle, and they create somewhat raised paint dots on the design sheets. It's a fun idea with colorful paints, but it is kind of simple so probably for younger kids rather than teenagers or older.
text_fidelity_b: Faber-Castell Do-Art Dot a Design Animals

LEGO Creator 3in1 Fire Dragon 31102 Building Kit, Cool Buildable Toy for Kids (234 Pieces) & Creator 3in1 Sports Car Toy 31100 Building Kit (134 Pieces) Having built some of the Lego Ninjago dragons lately, I can’t help but compare them to the Creator 3-in-1 Fire Dragon. I know it’s not a really fair comparison since they are two different themes, but my mind did it anyway. The Ninjago dragons look a bit cooler to me, but the Creator dragon doesn’t use any stickers … so it’s a draw in the end.

I think it’s weird the dragon doesn’t have any arms! He has little T-rex hands attached to his wings, but I wish he had arms so he looked cooler when standing up. It can be tricky to balance him on just his hind legs and tail, though it *is* possible.

As this is a 3-in-1 set, there are instruction books for two other builds, a saber-toothed tiger and a scorpion. I might like the tiger best of all, just because he looks a little derpy.

Overall, I like the 3-in-1 sets, since I think they show kids a different range of techniques, and how bricks can be repurposed from one build to another.

I was curious about diamond painting but didn’t want to commit to a big one, I didn’t know if I’d like it or not. This kit has 19 different princesses and superheroes to do, measuring about 2 to 3.5 inches tall and about 2 to 3 inches wide. So the figures are relatively small, about an hour’s worth of time to complete, depending on age and speed.

The back of the box includes basic instructions. This was my first time, so I also watched a video to better understand how to use the wax block (the box calls it “solid glue” which is an interesting translation).

The diamonds do not come in resealable baggies, which is a negative. The same colors are used from character to character. For example, many of the princesses use the same bright yellow for their hair. But if I do one princess today and another in the future, I have to put those yellow diamonds in a new baggie to store inbetween.

The baggies come in a long strip with perforations to tear them free -- be careful. In my experience, the baggies tore when I tried to separate them, so I cut them apart.

The different images can be cut apart. I recommend this, since you don’t want to remove the top plastic until you’re ready to paint with diamonds (the canvases are sticky underneath the plastic). Some of the princesses are very close together which does make cutting them apart a little tricky.

Battat - Deluxe Wooden Train – Classic Toy Train Set with Magnetic Trains, Tracks, Vehicles, Buildings & Accessories for Kids Aged 3 & Up (102Pc), Fits Thomas, Brio, Chuggington Trains are a classic toy. Most of them are electronic, high- tech in nature, and can be made to look and sound like an authentic train, in small scale of course. But there is also something to be said for a train that isn’t electronic and requires imagination more than anything. This is what you get with the Battat Deluxe Wooden Train.

This train set comes with track, train, and a large number of accessories. It’s easy to assemble the track because it interlocks with almost no effort. Setting up the accessories takes time, but this is perfect for the more imaginative child and parents will enjoy just sitting back and letting their youngster take over.

The quality level of this set is good and the pieces are made from wood. Once assembled, it covers about four feet by three feet of space, so it will fit on most tables. If you don’t have available table space to spare, just set it up on the floor instead. A smooth surface is best, of course, but a flat carpet may work, too.

With the train cars, they are held together by magnets and this is good enough for this type of train. One issue some people may have is with the track. The interlocking isn’t very secure and that means the track is easy to bump out of place. Metal tracks hold together better, but this isn’t a huge issue, really. Most kids won’t mind this aspect of the set up.

There are some really cool electronic trains on the market, but trains that require manual movements and that lack sound and other automated features can be just as fun. The Battat Deluxe Wooden Train is good for this purpose. It’s made with a good deal of quality in mind and it’s great for stimulating a child’s imagination.

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Games Words with Friends Luxe I love word games and I particularly like Scrabble. I have seen Words with Friends online and though I have not played it online I suspected this game would be a lot like Scrabble. It definitely is. It's a good game and can be a great addition to family game night.

Words with Friends is a crossword game where the goal is to create words and score points by strategically placing the words on the game board. The board has a number of bonus squares where extra points can be had - double word, triple word, double letter and triple letter. The player with the highest score at the end of the game wins. Each player gets 7 letter tiles (with point counts printed directly on the tiles) with which to make words. Play continues until all the tiles are used and all of the scoring opportunities are expended.

Game play as described above is just like Scrabble, but there are some differences. The score assigned to individual letters varies is little bit. The bonus squares are laid out differently too. Using all 7 letters in one turn results in a 35-point bonus, not 50.

The tiles are a glassy-looking orange color and are very aesthetically pleasing, even though they are simply plastic. The board itself is a two-piece creation and it clips together into one larger board. Assembly is simple.

I noticed a couple of flaws in this game, though these are not enough to lower my opinion of the game enough to matter. First, the board does clip together and turns nicely - on hard, flat surfaces. On carpet, the board can be a little uncooperative and can come apart. My second complaint is that the rules are so general that there is a little room for interpretation. People who have played Scrabble have a slight advantage - the unspecified rules are easy to fill in.

I especially like something printed on the box: "Your Smart Phone Unlocks Digital Features (phone not included)" Sorry, this made me laugh - I hope it's clear to everyone that there's no phone in the box...

Other than a touchy board and some slightly incomplete rules, this is a very fun game and is sure to be a hit on game night. My teenager and I have been playing and he's learning that I know more than he thought I did...
text_fidelity_b: Hasbro Games Words with Friends Luxe

It’s an interesting build, with some elements attached underneath (studs not on top), many added to the sides, and several specialized parts (e.g., canopy, bolt launchers). The finished build is solid, and provides a toy that’s fun to play with (even for adults).

The pod has room inside for all three minifigs (Rose, Finn, BB8). The pod canopy, rear compartment roof, and side storage compartment door lift off and go back on easily. The cockpit has holders for Finn’s and Rose’s weapons. The storage compartment has extra weapons.

The pod has a side turret gun that swivels for aiming when you turn the big knob at the back. The turret gun has a trigger that launches single rounds. The pod shoots long red bolts (rounded tips, not pointed) from underneath the cockpit. (Two special-to-the-kit bricks have springs inside that work as launchers). The pod feels good in your hand.

The kit takes two hours or less to build; it uses some Technic connectors in addition to standard bricks and plates. The instructions are crystal clear. There are quite a few stickers to add to the bricks, but the graphics are nice when all the stickers are in place.

This is a great small LEGO kit, one that I’ll be keeping for display and play.

text_fidelity_a:
Kubros Despicable Me Minion Building Kit I am a Lego fan, but I kept that in mind as I reviewed this, not wanting it to make my review unfair.
So, lets start with the kit. The pieces do not fit together as well as Lego pieces do. That’s not a huge thing, but it’s a little annoying with some of the steps.
I have to say that the instructions are much better than Lego ones –MegaBlox devised a very clear way to show what piece to put, and where to put it. That was nice. However, they lace the style Lego shows – if this were a Lego set, it would be hollow – allowing things to go inside it – this set is solid, no room inside for anything. The feet fall off easily, which gets old fast.

Plus there are many “special” bricks that will limit the owners ability to make other things out of the set. Although, that is moot if you have a sizable MegaBlox collection already.

The finished piece is nice – a little boxy – think Minions meets Minecraft.

My issue is the price though. If you look at Lego sets (aside from brand ones like Disney and some of the collectable ones) the cost is around 10c per brick.
This set works out at almost 30cents per brick. Three times the cost of a comparably sized Lego set.
The quality does not warrant that price. Despite the added value of the Despicable Me brand. If it was rounder, more interactive, or had stronger feet I would be inclines to give it a better score

If the shortcomings don’t bother you, and your life *needs* all things “Despicable Me” then you will enjoy this.
If someone else is paying for it, you will find it a bargain.

Otherwise I would recommend you get your Despicable Me and building set fix from a better product.

text_fidelity_a:
Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb. Most reviews mention the mind-boggling size of the model; I figured that it was because when we gain fatty tissue, it's distributed in a thin layer over our bodies, so seeing it as a lump would be surprising to most people.

     Even with the warnings, I was still shocked! It looked like it had to be 8-10 pounds, not a mere 5! And it FELT like 6-8 pounds...

After a while, I got curious as to why it seemed so disproportionately large. I'm aware that I consistently make terrible (truly awful) estimations of volumes, distances, and weights, so I measured it, just to get the actual numbers.

     My kitchen scale gave the model's mass as 5.293 pounds. That's a forgivable degree of error: 6%. Definitely closer than my awful guesstimate of 6-8 pounds.

     I used displacement to measure the volume as 11.75 cups. [I filled a container to overflowing with water. I added the model to displace some water, then removed the model. I carefully measured how much water I added to completely refill the container.]

     Google conversions gives 11.75 cups as being 169.6 in^3. Various sites list the volume of a pound of adipose tissue as being 29 in^3, 29.5 in^3, 30.08 in^3, and 30.42 in^3.

Using the model's volume and the lowest density, I calculate the model's representative mass as:
169.6 in^3 ÷ 30.42 in^3/lbs = 5.577 lbs

And using the highest density to calculate my model's "mass":
169.6 in^3 ÷ 29 in^3/lbs = 5.8 lbs (17% greater than 5 pounds, but well under my 8-10 pound guess.)

So whether you are measuring by weight or volume, the model is 6-17% oversized. That's far more accurate than seemed possible.

Obviously the manufacturer had to compromise between approximating the coloration, texture, pliablity, volume, and weight. I'm not a surgeon, so I'm clueless as to the accuracy of the coloration, texture, and pliablity. I am disappointed that the volume (which was the characteristic I was most interested in) was off by more than 5%.
text_fidelity_b: Nasco WA04313 Human Body Fat Replica, 5 lb.

SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is just one of dozens and dozens of slime toys intended to fascinate the young scientist in your home. The way most of these labs works is similar: Combine the included slime mix, if any exists, with a few household items like baking soda, vinegar, cornstarch, etc., and let the fun begin.

This slime toy works like the others in terms of the mixing, but it is also different than others, and I mean that in a good way. With this slime lab, the mixture is placed atop a motor that vibrates for greater effect. Kids can watch the colors and textures swirl around as the vibrations create some fun and very visual patterns. The instructions include 20 different recipes for slime and each can be made using items found in most kitchens.

What I probably like best about this slime lab is the lack of mess! Okay, there is some mess but in relative terms, the messiness is kept under control very well. The key difference is that, with most other slime labs my kids have used, messiness is encouraged. These other labs involve sticking hands in the slime, spreading it with your hands, and so on. This is messy and gross, and if multiple kids are involved, they often end up smearing it on each other, splattering it on the floors and more. There is no problem like that with SmartLab. The slime, for the most part, stays in the bowl, out of your way.

Educational toys are nice and SmartLab Toys It’s Alive Slime Lab is a toy that does get kids thinking and asking questions. My girls like it and have returned to it more than once, creating more slime and learning about household chemicals and how they react. It’s a good choice of toy that will keep kids entertained as they learn.
text_fidelity_b: SmartLab Toys It's Alive Slime Lab

The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure This is a 'cute' little toy. I like the expression on his face. We've had fun playing with it for the past couple weeks.

Some things that you might want to know about it if you're considering buying one.

The instructions suggest replacing the two AAA batteries when you take the figure out of the package - the two that come in it are for 'in-store' demonstration purposes. Opening the battery compartment I found that the supplied batteries are pretty decent alkaline ones. Still, I replaced the ones in mine as I hate it when batteries go dead in a device and then leak. Something to maybe mention - the battery compartment is secured with a screw, so that small hands can't get into it.

The tail on the rabbit acts as the on/off switch. There are three setting - On, Off, and Demo. In the demonstration mode the figure talks and the wheels turn for a few seconds and then stops. When in the On position, the figure says a phrase - the wheels go for awhile and then it stops and repeats the cycle. The figure has three wheels - two fixed wheels seem to drive it's motion and a third rotates to make the figure go in different directions. Our rabbit seems to have a habit of finding the nearest corner and parking itself in it. The figure's eyes move a bit when it's in running around (although it's hard to see with the way it's eyes are set).

The figure comes with a separate carrot prop. Which the rabbit is suppose to hold in it's one hand - ours kept dropping his. So I took a piece of the white string that had secured the toy to the package and tied the carrot to his hand- you can't really even see it.

The rabbit talks, and I know it's suppose to be Kevin Hart doing a 'cartoon' voice - but it's really hard to understand what it's suppose to be saying. Hopefully when the movie comes out the phrases will be more recognizable.

All in all I like this figure and I'm looking forward to seeing the movie.
text_fidelity_b: The Secret Life of Pets - Snowball Walking Talking Pets Figure

text_fidelity_a:
My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set This is a fun little train set for toddlers. The current product image is misleading, however, so I've posted photos to show how this nice little set comes. It comes in a handy carry bag with large plastic track pieces and two toys: Thomas the Tank Engine and Harold the Helicopter. Not quite sure why they include a helicopter to roll around a train track, but I suppose he is one of the more popular characters in Thomas' world. Regardless, they are both cute and large enough for a toddler to get his hands on and push around the track.

Thomas and Harold come attached to a piece of cardboard which keeps them in place. Before you go crazy on how to get these off - after a bit of struggling myself, I realized that all you have to do is rotate the plastic tab things that are holding them in place (located on the bottom). Just turn the tabs 90 degrees (doesn't matter which way) to free Thomas and Harold.

You will definitely need to help your put this together as the track pieces have a snug fit. they may loosen with time, however. There are instructions on how to put the track together, though I'm sure you can figure out your own unique layouts as well. The bridge pieces need a special little twist to put them together and remove them, so pay attention to that in the instructions, otherwise the rest simply snap together as you'd expect.

This is a really fun little set with a a nice carry bag to store all the pieces and even take the set with you on adventures. Little ones will love it!
text_fidelity_b: My First Thomas & Friends, On-the-Go Train Set

text_fidelity_a:
Craft-tastic – String Art Kit – Craft Kit Makes 2 Large String Art Canvases – Desserts Edition This is a fun arts & crafts item. It’s something that is fairly easy to do for a variety of ages. Though pictures always show girls doing this sort of thing. . . . I think lots of boys would enjoy it also.

This kit offers three “panels” for your designs. There are (sharp) pins you have to place into the foam base, so especially for younger kids, I would recommend either parents / adult do this. . . or. . . at least “supervise”. You’ll want to make sure to keep them in a “limited area” as well, so they don’t fall on the floor. This could be especially “painful” if one were to get “hidden” in carpet.

One thing I really like about something like this. . . . It gives kids something to do that’s fun. . . then. . . once it’s over. . . it’s over.

Hanging from the back is not all that easy. You might attach either some string, or a nice ribbon, to the top and hang it that way.

For Made in China, it’s a bit “pricey”, but not crazy expensive.
text_fidelity_b: Craft-tastic – String Art Kit – Craft Kit Makes 2 Large String Art Canvases – Desserts Edition

WireJewelry Double Barrel Rock Tumbler with (2) 3 Pound Capacity Drums My boys young boys have been rockhounds ever since we moved to Eastern Oregon three years ago. We thought we'd add the the thrill and enjoyment by getting them a tumbler to further explore the joys of rock hunting. There's a certain thrill of putting in raw stones that you think are "pretty", only to see their true beauty one they are polished.

We already have a single barrel WireJewelry tumbler and love it so much that we decided to grab this one to expand our capability. (There are LOTS of rocks here).

As before, assembly and setup was easy. Allowing one to have six total pounds of capacity is amazing. The heavy duty motor doesn't seem to be strained at all, even under full load, so it should last years. The barrel construction is very sturdy and we have never had even a minor leak. By design, they are very well sealed. While the noise level is not bad, I find it best to do my rock tumbling in the garage. The same hum in your house for weeks on end might just get to you.

This company is great for packaging kits, not only for the tumbling media, but for rocks as well. The media kids come numbered and labeled, so the process is super easy to follow. Tumbling is not a quick hobby... each batch can take weeks. Personally, I think that's part of the fun.

If you are thinking of getting into the hobby, I definitely recommend products from WireJewelry, I have yet to be disappointed in their products. Enjoy the treasure hunt!

text_fidelity_a:
Hasbro Gaming Sorry Spin My family has really enjoyed playing this updated version of an old favorite. The basic rules are the same as in the original Sorry! Each player has four pawns to move around the board from Start to Home. You draw a card to find out how many spaces you can move your game piece. Landing on another player's pawn sends them back to start as does the Sorry! card, just as in the classic version.

What's different about Sorry Spin is the spinning board. The center circle is the main board, with connecting circles for each color's home which fit together like gears. The challenge of the spinning board is your home is contantly changing position in relation to the main board. You may be just a few spaces away from reaching your home track when the board will spin and you will end up all the way across the board from your home.

It took about 5 minutes to assemble the game board, which seems very sturdy. We had some trouble spinning the board on a slick surface (wood table, counter top), but when we placed it on a placemat, it worked fine. A nice addition is a box that can be assembled and used to store the cards.

This is a great family game which is faster paced than the original version of the game due to the spinning board and a shorter path between start and home. Also any number gets a pawn out of start. text_fidelity_a:
LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit Holy Crap Yes! We are a family of Lego Maniacs and this set is wonderful. I have a fifteen year old and we recently got the newest Millenium Falcon and I had a realization that his abilities were quite beyond that set, and most sets out there, so I started looking at the expert and Technic sets. This set was perfect, it is a step up in challenge and scope from the standard sets. It was great to watch him to tear into the bags and deliberately build. Not only was it a little more challenging, but the scope if far more impressive. The set itself is huge, and the architectural elements are involved although somewhat repetitive.

We worked on this over several days and we are quite happy with the results. The build is detailed and has some very interesting pieces. Especially nice are the clock faces that are beautiful. The back printing on the clear disk gives them a gem like quality, they are sharp clean and wonderfully graphic. Absolutely beautiful. Also impressive are the scores of micro figures (usually found in Lego games.) Long term, I'm not sure that we will ever need this many tan microfigures on any build, but interesting piece. Also nice are the literally hundreds of architectural detail pieces from the little teeth pieces to the spires.

We actually looked up photos of Big Ben and we are astounded at the details. It is a wonderful representation of the end of the building. If I had anything negative to say about the build it would be that it is a bit of a façade for that end of Westminster. Which is forgivable given all the detail and how many pieces (and space) it would take to make the whole building.

All in all, this was an incredible build. I'll try to get the time lapse up when I can get it edited.
text_fidelity_b: LEGO Creator Expert 10253 Big Ben Building Kit

text_fidelity_a:
Elmer's Color Changing Liquid Glue | Makes Slime That Changes Color As You Play, Dark to Light Green, 5 oz. One of our kids has been on a slime kick of late, so we got this glue to add some dimension to the experience.

WHAT IS THIS GLUE LIKE?
This glue is a bit different on the label from the other color changing glue that we have used. It states that as you play, it will change in color from darker to lighter green. There is no odor and it is pretty standard type glue.

HOW DOES IT PERFORM WITH SLIME?
We used this with the Elmer's slime maker solution and got a nice slime. It makes a good consistency, and the slime is fun to play with if it is mixed at the right ratio.

DOES IT CHANGE COLOR?
That is where we have some issues. Perhaps because it is winter where we are testing this, but the slime does not want to change color unless it is really warm, something that only happens in sunlight after a while. Perhaps when it is warmer weather, or a really well heated room this will change more easily. For now, to get it to change to light green, we have to make it get REALLY warm in the sunlight in the window for a while.

THE BOTTOM LINE
This is a pretty green slime. It will change color if it gets really warm, but not as easily as we expected.

MY RATING
FOUR STARS. This does not change color that easily, so for that I have removed 1 star. It is still fun to play with as green slime, with the added bonus of changing color once in a great while when the conditions are just right, an added bonus.
text_fidelity_b: Elmer's Color Changing Liquid Glue | Makes Slime That Changes Color As You Play, Dark to Light Green, 5 oz.

text_fidelity_a:
CALOVER Gift Toys for Kids Cat Dog Remote Control Mock Rat Mouse Mice Prank Gag Funny Practical Joke Toy for Holiday Party Late last year, for a week or so, all 3 of our cats sat gathered around the stove in the kitchen just staring at it. I quickly figured that was probably NOT a good sign-that we likely had an uninvited guest in our home. A few days later, I was proven correct. Got up early one morning to take the dog out and there was a dead mouse by the front door waiting to greet me, with 2 of the 3 cats sitting close by, proud of what they had left for me. (I don't think I've ever screamed louder in my entire life than I did that morning! lolol-I did heap praise on them after I calmed down) Unfortunately, the cats were once again gathered around the stove watching...and a few days later, mouse #2 was waiting for us to clean up. (Thank God I didn't find that one)

As soon as I saw this cat toy, I immediately ordered it. Though one of our 3 cats who helped catch the mice has since gone to the Rainbow Bridge, I knew the other 2, Miss Piggy and Squeaky, would have loads of fun playing with this toy. (And if I'm being honest, I want to keep them in tip-top shape in case any further 'uninvited guests' find their way into our home! lol) The mouse (I see it more of a rat than a mouse) is nearly 11 inches long from the tip of the nose to the end of the tail. It has beady red eyes that light up. From a distance, I believe people (who don't know its fake) could mistaken it for a real mouse (rat). It has gray fur and what appears to be sharp teeth sticking out of its mouth. (The teeth are NOT sharp, they only appear that way) The mouse takes 3 AAA batteries (not included) and the remote controller takes 2 AAA batteries as well. (not included) The only assembly required is placing the batteries in the mouse and controller. A nice, small screwdriver comes with the toy, something I especially appreciate! (Works on my eyeglass hinges as well!) The controller allows you to move the mouse forward and backward. (Both of our young kids were able to operate the remote control without issue while we stood with them) It does work on carpet but works far better on flooring. As soon as we turned it on and began steering it around the room, 2 cats immediately popped out of their beds, their curiosity piqued. Both cats watched the mouse zip around the floor for a bit. As soon as it got close to Miss Piggy, she jumped and ran under the bed. lol. But Squeaky...he was far braver than Piggy and watched it up close. We'd stop it for awhile and he'd creep closer and closer to it, staring at it....and then we'd start it up again. lol. It was loads of fun to watch him with this toy. It certainly kept him entertained for quite some time! Piggy stayed hidden but she's a nosy cat...she'll get the hang of it before long.

This is a fun toy not only for cats but for cat owners to operate for their cats! We had loads of fun watching the cat's reaction. Its a great way for your cat to get some exercise as well. Very easy to operate also!

UPDATE******************

We got this out again tonight to play with. This time, the dog had more fun chasing it than the cats. However, after just under 15 minutes of use, it stopped working entirely! Even though I had used brand new batteries in the mouse and the controller when I first got it (a day ago), I replaced all 5 batteries. It does NOT work at all. Nothing happened to it. It did not fall, it didn't' crash, it was not damaged in any way, it simply stopped working altogether in the blink of an eye. And that's a darn shame because my cat AND dog had fun with it. Due to the fact that it stopped working entirely after just under 30 minutes of total use since we got it, and the fact we did nothing to break it/make it stop working, I've changed my rating/review of this item. I cannot recommend an item that stops working out of the blue as this did. For the minutes that it did work, my pets loved it. And we loved watching them have fun.
text_fidelity_b: CALOVER Gift Toys for Kids Cat Dog Remote Control Mock Rat Mouse Mice Prank Gag Funny Practical Joke Toy for Holiday Party

text_fidelity_a:
Klutz Bath and Body Activity Kit Multicolor, 9" Length x 1.75" Width x 9" Height When it comes to making things on our own, my household is a busy place with lots of creativity flowing. When we saw this kit, we could not wait to use it. Finally after waiting due to issues in our house which required a lot of remodeling, we were able to try this out. Let's see how it was..

WHAT IS THIS KIT LIKE?
This kit is one of our favorites. Being those who love color, we enjoyed the beautiful colored box. The box has a very detailed booklet on it which outlines every single project in the box and tells how to do the project. The photography is perfect and easy to read and follow. The layout and writing is perfect for using with children- both younger and older. There is not only an assortment of ingredients all carefully labeled and packaged, but there are little boxes and other decorative containers that you put together to give or display your creations in. I love that the bags are also labeled with what project it is good for and the page number in the booklet which is part of the box, so you won't lose it.

HOW DID OUR CREATIONS TURN OUT?
We had such fun with this. We enjoyed making the Bubble Bath Bon Bons most of all, and they really did work nicely in the tub. We have not done ALL of the projects yet, but the Bon Bons are the favorite so far- especially the marble method of mixing the colors. The little boxes that you put together are really cute and perfect to give as gifts. We also had fun with the lip mask.

ANY DRAWBACKS?
You will have to buy some fresh ingredients for this kit. That means that your treatments will be natural and safe for the face as well as fresh. Strawberry, lemon, avocado, banana, milk, honey, coconut milk, fine sugar or colored sugar, yogurt, and olive oil. Be prepared to have those on hand if you want to do the entire kit. We didn't mind though as we use these things in our home anyway, except for sugar, but I did have some on hand from a sugar scrub we experimented with in the past.

THE BOTTOM LINE
With all of the more unusual ingredients supplied, this kit is great fun to do. My daughter and I had a wonderful time with it. The colors, layout, and packaging are top notch. With the exception of having to provide quite a few fresh ingredients, this is easy and convenient but great fun when you finally do get to have your SPA day!

MY RATING
FIVE STARS! This can be used from young kids who are able to do this with supervision up to older kids- even late teens- who really want to have fun creating a spa day. I can also see using the principles used in this in the future creating a spa day for grandma or others that the kids want to reach out to for a special day.
text_fidelity_b: Klutz Bath and Body Activity Kit Multicolor, 9" Length x 1.75" Width x 9" Height

Nerf N-Strike Elite SlingStrike Slingshot We are a nerf house. Day glo foam nerf darts are lying on the floor in every room. I found one in the pantry, on top of a box of cheerios. We have a large box of guns, crossbows, blow dart guns and paper targets.

So this slingshot was eagerly awaited by the entire family. Like all nerf products it is sturdy and easy to use. It holds two darts which while not making it a rapid firing weapon, it does have a backup which is nice. It's kinda cool how it shoots and it was surprisingly accurate.

But it wasn't as cool as the nerf crossbow. There is something just so so awesome about holding a crossbow and shooting your husband in the butt that is lost with this slingshot.

I think a real sling shot would be cooler and a lot more deadly, of course, so not child friendly.

But for what it is, the novelty of the slingshot weapon is pretty awesome.
